newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S DEC YR/YR INFLATION TO DROP TO 17 PCT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S DEC YR/YR INFLATION TO DROP TO 17 PCT.

text.p: Hungary's December year on year inflation will drop to around 17 percent by December of 1997 and should average 18 percent for next year, Central Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi said on Tuesday.
"The December to December figure is expected to be around 17 percent. The average is rather 18 percent," Suranyi told Reuters following an appearance at an economic conference in Budapest.
Suranyi said the target appeared reachable because of recent declines in Hungary's inflation rate.
"It's not a really over-ambitious target. At the end of October we were at 21 (percent) and we are going to be 20 or 20.5 percent by the end of the year," he said.
"So the targeted drop is exactly four percent...and the average this year the average is going to be 23 to 23.5 percent," he added.

He acknowledged the rate was higher than the target of 20 percent average for the year agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as terms of a $387 million standby loan facility granted to Hungary in March.
"Well, that's the reality and I'm pretty sure that they will take it," Suranyi said.
